chunks: And with this chain of narration, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from his father, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Dawud, from his brother Abdillah, who said:
A man sent me to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), claiming that he would be startled in his sleep, seeing his wife coming to him, and he would shout until the neighbors heard.
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Go and tell him, 'You do not pay the Zakat.'
He said: 'Yes, by Allah, I do pay it.'
Tell him, 'If you do pay it, then you do not give it to its rightful recipients.'
ai.seo_question: Why did the Imam attribute the man's sleep disturbance to Zakat?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Thawab al-Amal*, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) diagnoses a man's sleep disturbances as a spiritual consequence of neglecting the specific conditions of Zakat, specifically its proper distribution to the deserving poor (*Fuqara* and *Masakin*). This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis that mere payment is insufficient; the validity of the act depends on fulfilling the jurisprudential criteria of *Istifa'* (selection) and *Infaq* (spending) to the correct recipients, thereby linking ritual purity with social justice.
